title: Exact four-dimensional projection quality of the OneTwo Sobol' table at 65,536 points
abstract: The quality parameter t of a base-2 digital net with 2^m points measures exact equidistribution in dyadic boxes, and for Sobol' sequences used in quasi-Monte Carlo integration and computer graphics the quality of low-dimensional projections is a practical bottleneck. The OneTwo construction of Bonneel, Coeurjolly, Iehl, and Ostromoukhov (ACM Transactions on Graphics, 2025) releases a 692-dimension direction-number table whose protected pairs (2k-1, 2k) have the (1,2) property, with acceptance targets t <= 3 through m <= 10 and t <= 4 through m <= 15 for the pair-aligned four-dimensional blocks. Theorem 1.1 of the preprint determines the next depth exactly: at m = 16, a complete batch of 65,536 points, every one of the 345 pair-aligned windows of the released table has exact four-dimensional t-value 4 when its first dimension is one of 1, 7, 31, 49, 67, 195, 225, 243, 373 and t-value 5 otherwise, so the t <= 4 guarantee extends to m = 16 in exactly nine windows and fails in the other 336, each failure witnessed by an empty dyadic box of volume 2^-12 in that projection. The standard star-discrepancy bound for the projection is 299/4096 at t = 4 and 29/256 at t = 5. This Lean development proves the theorem in rank form with the released table embedded as one 256-bit literal per dimension: for every window, every four-part composition at the threshold total selects independent generator rows over F_2 and some composition one total higher does not, and the distribution is 9 windows at t = 4 and 336 at t = 5. The worked block, dimensions 25 to 28, keeps its separate explicit certificate (t = 5, with every smaller threshold refuted). All checks are 16-column XOR row reductions reduced by kernel decide with no native evaluation. The digital-net rank criterion, the discrepancy bound, and the authentication of the upstream table remain informal.
